questions.question: You are tasked with creating a controller block for a custom single‑purpose processor that will replace an analog temperature‑compensation circuit. Which design benefit from the provided context should you primarily emphasize to justify using a software‑based controller?

options.B: Ability to upgrade control logic without hardware changes

questions.explanation:
The context states that software control “can be upgraded or modified easily (change gains, modes, or algorithms without hardware changes)” and replaces expensive analog hardware [Page 178].

---

questions.question: When designing the FSM for a dual‑purpose processor that handles both signal filtering and AES encryption, which design step should be performed immediately after defining the instruction set according to the design process described?

options.B: Creating an FSMD (Finite‑State Machine with Datapath)

questions.explanation:
The design flow lists “choosing or defining the instruction set, followed by creating an FSMD” as the next step [Page 105].

---

questions.question: In the controller block of a custom processor intended for motor‑control (an SSP), which of the following components is most likely to be part of the datapath that the control unit will orchestrate?

options.B: Dedicated PWM generator and ADC interface

questions.explanation:
Domain‑specific processors such as motor‑control ICs include specialized functional blocks; the controller must manage these datapath elements, as implied by the description of SSP/SPP processors for motor control [Page 40].

---

questions.question: Suppose you need to adapt the controller of a custom processor to compensate for aging effects in a plant. Which characteristic from the context allows you to implement this adaptation without redesigning hardware?
questions.explanation:
The context highlights “Programmability – Control logic can be upgraded or modified easily… Adaptability can automatically adjust to changes in the plant” [Page 178].

---

questions.question: You are drawing a block diagram for a controller of a single‑purpose processor that implements an AES encryption engine. Which of the following connections is essential according to the controller‑datapath relationship described?

options.A: Direct link from controller to external flash memory only
options.B: Control signals from the controller to the encryption datapath units (e.g., substitution boxes)
options.C: Bidirectional bus between controller and Wi‑Fi module
options.D: No connection; the controller operates independently of the datapath

questions.explanation:
The controller/FSM “is developed” after datapath components are designed and connected to the control unit, implying control signals must drive the encryption datapath [Page 105].

---

questions.question: When comparing an MPU (e.g., Intel Atom) with an MCU (e.g., STM32) for implementing a custom controller block, which statement correctly applies the distinction provided in the context?

options.A: An MPU includes on‑chip memory and I/O, making it ideal for single‑purpose control.
options.B: An MCU requires external memory to implement the controller FSM.
options.C: An MPU consists of CPU only and needs external memory, whereas an MCU integrates CPU, memory, and I/O on one chip, simplifying controller integration.
options.D: Both MPU and MCU have identical architectures for controller design.

questions.explanation:
The table differentiates MPU as “CPU only; needs external memory” and MCU as “CPU + memory + I/O on one chip” [Page 43].

---

questions.question: In designing a finite‑state machine for a dual‑purpose processor that must switch between DSP filtering and general‑purpose computation, which design principle from the context helps you decide the sequencing of states?

options.A: Prioritize high‑level OS tasks before low‑level DSP tasks.
options.B: Use the FSMD approach to integrate datapath operations with control states.
options.C: Implement a separate controller for each purpose without interaction.
options.D: Rely on external peripherals to manage state transitions.

questions.explanation:
The context recommends creating an FSMD (Finite‑State Machine with Datapath) to coordinate control and datapath functions [Page 105].

---

questions.question: A custom processor’s controller must be updated to change the gain of a motor‑control loop after deployment. Which of the following actions aligns with the “Adaptability” benefit described?

options.A: Replace the silicon chip with a new version.
options.B: Re‑flash the controller firmware with new gain values.
options.C: Add an external analog gain stage.
options.D: Increase the clock frequency of the processor.

questions.explanation:
Adaptability allows the controller to “automatically adjust to changes… (e.g., due to aging, temperature, or wear)” via software updates [Page 178].

---

questions.question: While proposing a block diagram for a controller of a custom single‑purpose processor intended for an AES encryption engine, which of the following blocks must be included to satisfy the “control‑logic” role defined in the context?

options.A: Instruction decoder, control FSM, and datapath interconnect.
options.B: Power‑management unit and external flash only.

questions.explanation:
The controller block comprises the control unit (FSM) that drives the datapath; the instruction decoder and interconnect are typical parts of a custom controller design as implied by the design flow [Page 105].

---

questions.question: If a designer chooses a domain‑specific processor (DSP) like the TI C6000 for a custom controller block, which characteristic from the context justifies this selection for a signal‑processing application?

options.B: Optimization for a particular application or domain.
options.C: Requirement of external memory for all operations.

questions.explanation: DSPs and other domain‑specific processors are “Optimized for a particular application or domain” [Page 40].
